chunks: We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Abdullah bin Hasan, the Teacher, from Ahmad bin Ali al-Esbahani, from Ibrahim bin Muhammad al-Thaqafi, that he said: I was informed by Ahmad bin Abi Umar al-Nahdi, that he said: I was told by my father, from Muhammad bin Marwan, from Muhammad bin Sa'ib, from Abu Saleh, from Ibn Abbas
with regards to the saying of Him, Exalted and Glorious is He: «Peace be upon the Family of Yasin.» He said: Upon the Family of Muhammad, peace be upon them.

key_terms.آل مُحَمَّد: The Family of Muhammad, referring to the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.آل يَاسِين: The Family of Yasin, interpreted here as the Family of the Prophet Muhammad
key_terms.ابْنِ عَبَّاس: Ibn Abbas, a prominent companion of the Prophet known for his Quranic exegesis
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Exalted and Glorious is He, an honorific phrase used when quoting or referring to God

ai.seo_question: Who does 'Al-Yasin' refer to in the Quran according to Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, this hadith presents a prominent Shia interpretation where 'Yasin' is understood as a title for the Prophet Muhammad, thereby identifying 'Al-Yasin' as the Ahl al-Bayt. This exegesis, traced through the chain of the Prophet’s companion Ibn Abbas, underscores the divine bestowal of peace specifically upon the Prophet’s household, reinforcing their unique spiritual status in Shia theology.

en.basel-kadem: 4.	We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Abdullah bin Hasan, the Teacher, from Ahmad bin Ali al-Esbahani, from Ibrahim bin Muhammed al-Thaqafi, that he said: I was informed by Ahmad bin Abi Umra al-Nahdi, that he said: I was told by my father, from Muhammed bin Marwan, from Muhammed bin Sa’ib, from Abu Saleh, from Ibn Abbas,
with regards to the saying of Him, Exalted and Glorious is He: «Peace be upon the Family of Yasin.» [1] He said: Upon the Family of Muhammed, peace be upon them.
